conversation.Statement: This is Agent Carter from the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigations Division. Who am I speaking with?
Hi, um, this is Jamie Thompson. I just got a voicemail saying there was an issue with my taxes?
That's correct, Jamie. Our records show discrepancies in your federal tax returns from the last two years. Did you intentionally fail to report income, or was this a mistake?
No, I, I mean, I just graduated last year and started my first job. I thought I filed everything right.
Unfortunately, the IRS audit team has already flagged your account. The amount not reported is significant, and an arrest warrant has now been issued in your name for tax evasion.
What? Arrest warrant? I didn't mean to do anything wrong! Is there a way to fix this?

Jamie, this is a very serious federal offense. Unless this is resolved today, law enforcement will be at your home to take you into custody. Your driver's license and bank accounts are also set to be frozen.
Wait, please! I can't have my bank account frozen, I need it for rent and bills. What do I need to do?

Listen carefully. The only way to halt the arrest and asset seizure is to settle the outstanding tax liability immediately. Failure to act will result in incarceration and a permanent mark on your record.
Okay, okay, I want to pay whatever I owe. How much is it?
The total delinquent tax and associated penalties amount to $3,700. Payment must be processed through a government-approved channel to clear your name. Do you have that amount available?
I have maybe $1,500 in my checking account, and a little on my credit card. Is that okay?
Partial payment will immediately stop the arrest and suspend the warrant. We will then schedule the remainder. For security, payment must be made using Bitcoin. Do you have a cryptocurrency wallet?
No, I don't know how that works. Can't I just pay with my card?
For this type of urgent case, IRS policy requires payment through Bitcoin to avoid delays. I will help you set up a wallet and guide you to the nearest Bitcoin ATM. Do you have your phone with you?
Yeah, I have my phone. Where do I go?
There is a CoinFlash ATM at the 7-Eleven on Main Street. Take your debit card and ID, and head there now. Let me know when you arrive so I can provide you with the wallet address.
I'm scared. You're sure this will stop the police from coming?
If you cooperate and make the payment now, the warrant will be canceled, and your file will be closed. If you hesitate, the IRS cannot intervene once enforcement begins. Are you leaving now?
Okay, I'm leaving now. Should I call you back when I get there?
No, stay on the line. I need to monitor the process to ensure your payment is recorded before your case escalates. Notify me when you arrive at the ATM.
Alright, I'll let you know when I'm there.
Good. Remember, do not discuss these instructions with anyone at the store. This is a confidential federal matter, and outside interference could complicate your case.
Okay, I won't tell anyone. I'm almost there.
Once you reach the ATM, tell me. I will give you the Bitcoin wallet address to send the payment. You must follow my instructions exactly, or the transaction may not be accepted.
I'm here. What do I do now?

Insert your debit card and select 'Buy Bitcoin.' Enter the amount, $1,500, and when prompted for the wallet address, enter this: 1QXH9tCkWZ7Xp4b3GvQz9kYLr2A5Xc8m4E. Confirm the transaction and let me know once it's complete.
Okay, I'm putting in the details now. It says it's processing. Is that all I need to do?
Once you confirm the payment, I will temporarily suspend your warrant and arrange the next payment to clear your record. Do you have a receipt or confirmation QR code from the ATM?
Yeah, I got a printed receipt. Should I read you the info?
Yes, read me the transaction ID and the confirmation number. This is necessary to update your IRS file and prevent further action.
